1.explanation: The shared ECMA-Script helper (src/languages/lib/ecmascript.js) maintains the list of built-in globals and types for JS/TS. BigInt, BigInt64Array and BigUint64Array are currently missing from that list, so the grammar never tags them as built_in. Both the JavaScript (javascript.js) and the TypeScript (typescript.js) language definitions pull in this shared list, so updating ecmascript.js (and ensuring the patches flow through in the JS and TS modules) will restore the correct highlighting.

2.explanation:
1. src/languages/lib/ecmascript.js – This is the core built-in keyword list for ECMAScript. It currently lists Number, String, Boolean, Symbol, Object, Function, etc., but omits BigInt, BigInt64Array, and BigUint64Array. Those identifiers need to be added to the built_in keyword group here.  
2. src/languages/javascript.js – This file imports and re-exports the ECMAScript definition, so it must remain in sync with any additions made in lib/ecmascript.js.  
3. src/languages/typescript.js – TypeScript mode extends the ECMAScript core keywords, including typed arrays and global objects. It should likewise include the new BigInt-related built-ins so that TS highlighting also picks them up.
2.bug_scenario: When writing JavaScript (ECMAScript) code that uses the BigInt built-in type (for example, let bi = BigInt('1');), highlight.js fails to recognize and highlight “BigInt” (and similarly “BigInt64Array” and “BigUint64Array”) as built-in types. The screenshots show “BigInt” remaining unstyled in the actual output, whereas it should receive the same built-in type styling applied to “Number” and other globals.
